title: Linked views with crosstalk
text: Wrap data SharedData pipe go_figure(). Formula properties (x = ~gdpPercap) evaluated data, data frame, trace built rows linked: every point carries row’s key. Click point select country: points twelve years highlighted, showing path. Double-click clear; hold shift add countries. key says rows belong together; default data’s row names (one key per row). Views sharing group (default, one per SharedData; set SharedData$new(group = )) linked. Without highlight(), linked figure selects click clears double-click.
code: SharedData$new(gap, key = ~country) |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~gdpPercap, y = ~lifeExp, text = ~country, mode = "markers") |>   update_layout(xaxis = go_xaxis(type = "log")) |>   highlight(color = "red")

title: Linked views with crosstalk
text: figure made SharedData, SharedDatas group keys, view selection. 2007’s rows years’ rows linked group “countries”: selecting countries box lasso first plot shows histories second, attrs_selected() draws selected points lines. Clicking point history plot selects country .

what: Linking traces built from other data
title: Linked views with crosstalk
text: set_crosstalk_keys() links traces whose values don’t come SharedData’s rows, summaries: give keys trace’s points group join. points keyed continent, bar chart countries per continent linked , clicking bar selects every country continent (clicking point selects continent): simple = TRUE, trace stands keys whole, marks can’t split points, line summarising group. continent’s average life expectancy line standing countries: clicking line selects plot . line highlighted countries selected.
code: by_continent <- SharedData$new(gap, key = ~continent) countries <- gap[year == 2007, .N, by = continent]  continent_bars <- go_figure() |>   add_bar(x = countries$continent, y = countries$N) |>   set_crosstalk_keys(countries$continent, group = by_continent$groupName()) |>   update_layout(height = 300, yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "countries")) |>   highlight(color = "red")  continent_points <- by_continent |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~gdpPercap, y = ~lifeExp, text = ~country, mode = "markers") |>   update_layout(height = 350, xaxis = go_xaxis(type = "log")) |>   highlight(color = "red")  htmltools::tagList(as_widget(continent_bars), as_widget(continent_points)) by_country2 <- SharedData$new(gap, key = ~country)  averages <- go_figure() for (cont in sort(unique(gap$continent))) {   d <- gap[continent == cont, .(lifeExp = mean(lifeExp)), by = year]   averages <- averages |>     add_scatter(x = d$year, y = d$lifeExp, mode = "lines+markers", name = cont) |>     set_crosstalk_keys(unique(gap[continent == cont, country]),                        group = by_country2$groupName(),                        traces = length(averages$data) + 1L, simple = TRUE) } # plotly.js reports clicks on a line's points: let a click near the line count averages <- averages |>   update_layout(height = 350, hoverdistance = 50, title = "Average by continent") |>   highlight(color = "red")  country_points <- by_country2 |>   go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = ~year, y = ~lifeExp, text = ~country, mode = "markers") |>   update_layout(height = 300, title = "Countries") |>   highlight(color = "red")  htmltools::tagList(as_widget(averages), as_widget(country_points))

title: Linked views with crosstalk
text: Subplots: traces added several cells (add_scatter(..., row = 1, col = "")) linked. set_crosstalk_keys() uses trace indices, call adding traces links. Animation: animation frame’s traces carry keys, set set_crosstalk_keys(). widgets: crosstalk-compatible widget, DT tables leaflet maps, can share group. Trace types: selection events need traces points (scatter, bar, histogram, box, maps, …); plotly.js reports clicks hovers line’s points, . Heatmaps, pies aggregating traces can’t selected point point. Shiny: crosstalk works without server; Shiny, event_data() also reports selections, SharedData selections can read <SharedData>$selection(). Size: keys sent strings, one per point; many thousands points, short keys keep pages small.

# one panel per case; x: values plotted, y: the measurement metric_chart <- function(col, label) { # res is sorted by case, size and variant, so each panel's sizes appear in order d <- res[, .(variant, case, label, value = get(col))] # "10 × 100,000" on two lines, so the labels stay horizontal d[, label := sub("10 × ", "10 ×
", label, fixed = TRUE)] cases <- levels(res$case) # R in blues, Python in oranges; the darkest of each is the float32 variant colors <- c(release = "#6baed6", core_backend = "#2171b5", go_figure_f32 = "#08306b", plotly_py = "#fd8d3c", plotly_py_f32 = "#a63603") fig <- make_subplots(rows = 1, cols = length(cases), subplot_titles = cases, horizontal_spacing = 0.02) for (j in seq_along(cases)) { for (v in variants) { dv <- d[case == cases[[j]] & variant == v] if (!nrow(dv)) next fig <- add_bar( fig, x = dv$label, y = dv$value, name = v, legendgroup = v, showlegend = j == 1, marker = go_bar_marker(color = colors[[v]]), row = 1, col = j ) } } fig |> # little margin around the panels (room below for the labels' descenders), # legend above them update_layout( barmode = "group", template = get_template("plotly_white"), margin = go_margin(l = 65, r = 5, t = 25, b = 20), legend = go_legend(orientation = "h", y = 1.08, yanchor = "bottom", x = 0) ) |> # each panel its own sizes, as categories: every bar the same width update_xaxes(type = "category") |> # one y axis shared by the panels, from 0 update_yaxes(matches = "y", rangemode = "tozero") |> update_yaxes(title = label, row = 1, col = 1) |> partial_bundle("auto") } metric_chart("build_sec", "build + write (s)") metric_chart("load_sec", "load (s)") metric_chart("html_mb", "HTML (MB)") metric_chart("peak_renderer_mb", "peak renderer (MB)") metric_chart("js_heap_mb", "JS heap after load (MB)") metric_chart("export_sec", "PNG export (s)")

dir.create(release_lib, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)   install.packages("plotly", lib = release_lib, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org",                    type = "source", dependencies = FALSE) } libs <- list(release = release_lib, core_backend = core_lib, go_figure_f32 = core_lib) python <- params$python cases <- rbindlist(list(   data.table(case = "timeseries", size = unlist(params$ts_sizes), values = as.integer(unlist(params$ts_sizes))),   data.table(case = "multiseries", size = unlist(params$ms_sizes), values = as.integer(unlist(params$ms_sizes) * 10)),   data.table(case = "heatmap", size = unlist(params$hm_sizes), values = as.integer(unlist(params$hm_sizes)^2)) )) cases[, file := file.path(wd, "data", sprintf("%s-%d.bin", case, size))] set.seed(2024) for (i in seq_len(nrow(cases))) {   n <- cases$size[i]   v <- if (cases$case[i] == "timeseries") {     cumsum(rnorm(n))   } else if (cases$case[i] == "multiseries") {     as.vector(apply(matrix(rnorm(n * 10), n), 2, cumsum))   } else {     s <- seq(0, 6 * pi, length.out = n)     as.vector(outer(sin(s), cos(s)) + rnorm(n * n, sd = 0.1))   }   writeBin(v, cases$file[i], endian = "little") } figures <- list(   release = list(     timeseries = function(t, y) plot_ly(x = t, y = y, type = "scattergl", mode = "lines"),     multiseries = function(d) {       p <- plot_ly(d, x = ~t)       for (col in names(d)[-1]) {         p <- add_trace(p, y = d[[col]], name = col, type = "scattergl", mode = "lines")       }       p     },     heatmap = function(z) plot_ly(z = z, type = "heatmap")   ),   go_figure_f32 = list(     timeseries = function(t, y) {       go_figure() |> add_scattergl(x = t, y = as_float32(y), mode = "lines")     },     multiseries = function(d) {       fig <- go_figure()       for (col in names(d)[-1]) {         fig <- add_scattergl(fig, x = d$t, y = as_float32(d[[col]]), name = col, mode = "lines")       }       fig     },     heatmap = function(z) go_figure() |> add_heatmap(z = as_float32(z))   ) ) # go_figure() figures load the smallest plotly.js bundle with their trace types figures$go_figure_f32 <- lapply(figures$go_figure_f32, function(make) {   function(...) partial_bundle(make(...)) }) # the same plot_ly() code, run with the development plotly figures$core_backend <- figures$release  # how each variant writes its page writers <- list(   release = function(p, file) htmlwidgets::saveWidget(p, file, selfcontained = FALSE, libdir = "lib"),   core_backend = function(p, file) plotly.core::write_html(p, file, selfcontained = FALSE, libdir = "lib"),   go_figure_f32 = function(fig, file) write_html(fig, file, selfcontained = FALSE, libdir = "lib") ) # how each variant exports a static image, with its package's save_image(): # Kaleido (via reticulate) for the CRAN release, Chrome via chromote for # plotly.core (plot_ly() in the development plotly uses plotly.core's). Each # keeps its browser running between images: plotly.core does by itself; # Kaleido is started as a persistent server (by default it starts a browser # for every image, which is slower and failed for some images here), with the # CRAN release's own plotly.js exporters <- list(   release = local({     started <- FALSE     function(p, file) {       if (!started) {         reticulate::import("kaleido")$start_sync_server(           plotlyjs = system.file("htmlwidgets", "lib", "plotlyjs", "plotly-latest.min.js", package = "plotly"),           silence_warnings = TRUE         )         started <<- TRUE       }       plotly::save_image(p, file)     }   }),   core_backend = function(p, file) plotly::save_image(p, file),   go_figure_f32 = function(fig, file) plotly.core::save_image(fig, file) ) import gc, json, sys, time import os import numpy as np, pandas as pd, plotly, plotly.io as pio, plotly.graph_objects as go import kaleido # Kaleido with plotly.py's own plotly.js (offline), kept running between images plotlyjs = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(plotly.__file__), "package_data", "plotly.min.js") pio.defaults.plotlyjs = plotlyjs kaleido.start_sync_server(plotlyjs=plotlyjs, silence_warnings=True)  variant, cases_file, reps, outdir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4] f32 = variant == "plotly_py_f32"  def timeseries(t, y):     return go.Figure(go.Scattergl(x=t, y=y, mode="lines"))  def multiseries(t, Y):     fig = go.Figure()     for j in range(Y.shape[1]):         fig.add_trace(go.Scattergl(x=t, y=Y[:, j], name=f"y{j + 1:02d}", mode="lines"))     return fig  def heatmap(z):     return go.Figure(go.Heatmap(z=z))  out = [] for case in json.load(open(cases_file)):     n, kind = case["size"], case["case"]     v = np.fromfile(case["file"], dtype="<f8")     if f32:         v = v.astype(np.float32)     if kind == "timeseries":         args = (pd.date_range("2024-01-01", periods=n, freq="s"), v)         make = timeseries     elif kind == "multiseries":         args = (pd.date_range("2024-01-01", periods=n, freq="s"), v.reshape((n, 10), order="F"))         make = multiseries     else:         args = (v.reshape((n, n), order="F"),)         make = heatmap     page = f"{outdir}/{kind}-{n}.html"     save = lambda: make(*args).write_html(page, include_plotlyjs="directory", full_html=True)     save()  # warm-up; also the page the browser loads     fig, png = make(*args), f"{outdir}/{kind}-{n}.png"     fig.write_image(png)  # warm-up     for rep in range(reps):         gc.collect()         t0 = time.perf_counter()         save()         t1 = time.perf_counter()         fig.write_image(png)         out.append(dict(variant=variant, case=kind, size=n, rep=rep + 1,                         build_sec=t1 - t0, export_sec=time.perf_counter() - t1)) kaleido.stop_sync_server(silence_warnings=True) json.dump(out, sys.stdout) r_worker <- function(variant, fns, write, export, cases, reps, outdir) {   suppressPackageStartupMessages(     if (variant == "go_figure_f32") library(plotly.core) else library(plotly)   )   dir.create(outdir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)   out <- list()   for (i in seq_len(nrow(cases))) {     n <- cases$size[i]     v <- readBin(cases$file[i], "double", n = cases$values[i], endian = "little")     t <- as.POSIXct("2024-01-01", tz = "UTC") + seq_len(n) - 1     if (cases$case[i] == "timeseries") {       args <- list(t = t, y = v)     } else if (cases$case[i] == "multiseries") {       y <- matrix(v, n, 10, dimnames = list(NULL, sprintf("y%02d", 1:10)))       args <- list(d = data.table::data.table(t = t, y))     } else {       args <- list(z = matrix(v, n, n))     }     make <- fns[[cases$case[i]]]     page <- file.path(outdir, sprintf("%s-%d.html", cases$case[i], n))     save <- function() write(do.call(make, args), page)     save() # warm-up; also the page the browser loads     # static image export of a figure made beforehand, so only the export is timed     fig <- do.call(make, args)     png <- file.path(outdir, sprintf("%s-%d.png", cases$case[i], n))     export(fig, png) # warm-up     for (rep in seq_len(reps)) {       gc()       out[[length(out) + 1]] <- list(         variant = variant, case = cases$case[i], size = n, rep = rep,         build_sec = system.time(save())[["elapsed"]],         export_sec = system.time(export(fig, png))[["elapsed"]]       )     }   }   data.table::rbindlist(out) }  # Kaleido (for the CRAN release) runs in the benchmark's Python, which also # has plotly; ~/.Renviron is skipped, as it may point reticulate elsewhere worker_env <- c(callr::rcmd_safe_env(), RETICULATE_PYTHON = python, R_ENVIRON_USER = tempfile()) build_r <- rbindlist(lapply(names(figures), function(v) {   callr::r(r_worker, list(v, figures[[v]], writers[[v]], exporters[[v]], cases, reps, file.path(pages_dir, v)),            libpath = c(libs[[v]], .libPaths()), env = worker_env) })) cases_json <- file.path(wd, "cases.json") jsonlite::write_json(cases[, .(case, size, file)], cases_json) build_py <- rbindlist(lapply(c("plotly_py", "plotly_py_f32"), function(v) {   outdir <- file.path(pages_dir, v)   dir.create(outdir, showWarnings = FALSE)   res <- system2(python, c(shQuote(file.path(wd, "bench.py")), v, shQuote(cases_json), reps,                            shQuote(outdir)), stdout = TRUE)   as.data.table(jsonlite::fromJSON(paste(res, collapse = ""))) })) build <- rbindlist(list(build_r, build_py)) # one page per variant and case size pages <- CJ(variant = variants, i = seq_len(nrow(cases)), sorted = FALSE)[   , c(.(variant = variant), cases[i, .(case, size, values)])] pages[, path := sprintf("%s/%s-%d.html", variant, case, size)] pages[, html_mb := file.size(file.path(pages_dir, path)) / 1e6] (function () {   var B = window.__bench = { done: false };   function finish() {     if (B.end != null) return;     B.end = performance.now();     requestAnimationFrame(function () {       setTimeout(function () { B.painted = performance.now(); B.done = true; }, 0);     });   }   // plotly.js 3+ exports are read-only, so the wrapper is a new object   // inheriting from Plotly, with timed newPlot()/react()/plot()   function wrap(P) {     if (!P || P.__benchWrapped) return P;     var W = Object.create(P);     ["newPlot", "react", "plot"].forEach(function (k) {       var orig = P[k];       if (typeof orig !== "function") return;       W[k] = function () {         if (B.start == null) B.start = performance.now();         var r = orig.apply(P, arguments);         Promise.resolve(r).then(finish, function (e) { B.error = String(e); B.done = true; });         return r;       };     });     W.__benchWrapped = true;     return W;   }   var plotly;   Object.defineProperty(window, "Plotly", {     configurable: true,     get: function () { return plotly; },     set: function (v) { plotly = wrap(v); }   });   window.addEventListener("error", function (e) { B.error = String(e.message); B.done = true; }); })(); hook_js <- paste(readLines(file.path(wd, "hook.js")), collapse = "\n") chrome <- chromote::Chromote$new()  # serve the pages over HTTP from localhost port <- httpuv::randomPort() server <- callr::r_bg(function(dir, port) httpuv::runStaticServer(dir, port = port, browse = FALSE),                       list(pages_dir, port)) for (i in 1:50) {   if (!inherits(try(suppressWarnings(readLines(sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d/", port), n = 1)),                     silent = TRUE), "try-error")) break   Sys.sleep(0.1) }  # samples the largest renderer process's memory (RSS) every 20 ms until killed sampler <- function(browser_pid, out) {   peak <- 0   writeLines("0", out) # started   repeat {     procs <- try(ps::ps_children(ps::ps_handle(browser_pid), recursive = TRUE), silent = TRUE)     if (!inherits(procs, "try-error")) {       for (p in procs) {         rss <- try({           if (any(grepl("--type=renderer", ps::ps_cmdline(p), fixed = TRUE))) ps::ps_memory_info(p)[["rss"]] else 0         }, silent = TRUE)         if (is.numeric(rss) && rss > peak) {           peak <- rss           writeLines(format(peak, scientific = FALSE), out)         }       }     }     Sys.sleep(0.02)   } } browser_pid <- chrome$get_browser()$get_process()$get_pid()  measure_page <- function(url, timeout = 300) {   s <- chromote::ChromoteSession$new(parent = chrome, width = 1000, height = 600)   on.exit(s$close(), add = TRUE)   s$Network$enable()   s$Network$setCacheDisabled(cacheDisabled = TRUE)   s$Page$enable() # needed for the injected script to run   s$Page$addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument(source = hook_js)   peak_file <- tempfile()   smp <- callr::r_bg(sampler, list(browser_pid, peak_file))   on.exit(smp$kill(), add = TRUE)   # wait for the sampler to start   for (i in 1:100) if (file.exists(peak_file)) break else Sys.sleep(0.05)   Sys.sleep(0.1)   s$Page$navigate(url, wait_ = FALSE) # large pages can take a while to commit   t0 <- Sys.time()   repeat {     done <- s$Runtime$evaluate("!!(window.__bench && window.__bench.done)", timeout_ = timeout)$result$value     if (isTRUE(done)) break     if (difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs") > timeout) stop("timed out loading ", url)     Sys.sleep(0.05)   }   Sys.sleep(0.3)   smp$kill()   b <- jsonlite::fromJSON(s$Runtime$evaluate(     "JSON.stringify(Object.assign({}, window.__bench, {js_bytes: performance.getEntriesByType('resource')        .filter(e => /\\.js$/.test(e.name)).reduce((a, e) => a + e.encodedBodySize, 0)}))"   )$result$value)   if (!is.null(b$error)) stop(url, ": ", b$error)   s$HeapProfiler$collectGarbage()   heap <- s$Runtime$getHeapUsage()   data.table(     load_sec = b$painted / 1000,     newplot_sec = (b$end - b$start) / 1000,     js_mb = b$js_bytes / 1e6,     peak_renderer_mb = as.numeric(readLines(peak_file, warn = FALSE)) / 1e6,     js_heap_mb = (heap$usedSize + if (is.null(heap$backingStorageSize)) 0 else heap$backingStorageSize) / 1e6   ) }  restart_chrome <- function() {   try(chrome$close(), silent = TRUE)   chrome <<- chromote::Chromote$new()   browser_pid <<- chrome$get_browser()$get_process()$get_pid() } # on a failure (e.g. Chrome not responding), restart Chrome and try the page # once more; a page that fails twice (e.g. too large to load) is recorded as # missing values, and not tried again in later rounds failed <- character() measure_retry <- function(url) {   missing <- data.table(load_sec = NA_real_, newplot_sec = NA_real_, js_mb = NA_real_,                         peak_renderer_mb = NA_real_, js_heap_mb = NA_real_)   if (url %in% failed) return(missing)   for (attempt in 1:2) {     r <- tryCatch(measure_page(url), error = identity)     if (!inherits(r, "error")) return(r)     message("attempt ", attempt, " at ", url, " failed: ", conditionMessage(r))     restart_chrome()   }   failed <<- c(failed, url)   missing }  set.seed(1) browser <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(reps), function(rep) {   # shuffle the page order each round, so drift doesn't favour a variant   rbindlist(lapply(sample(nrow(pages)), function(i) {     cbind(pages[i, .(variant, case, size)], rep = rep,           measure_retry(sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d/%s", port, pages$path[i])))   })) })) server$kill() r_versions <- function(lib) {   callr::r(function() {     js_version <- function(pkg, file) {       f <- system.file("htmlwidgets", "lib", "plotlyjs", file, package = pkg)       if (!nzchar(f)) return(NA_character_)       head <- readChar(f, 500)       sub("^v", "", regmatches(head, regexpr("v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+", head)))     }     # the development plotly draws with plotly.core's plotly.js     uses_core <- grepl("plotly.core", utils::packageDescription("plotly")$Imports, fixed = TRUE)     list(       plotly = as.character(utils::packageVersion("plotly")),       plotly.core = if (uses_core) as.character(utils::packageVersion("plotly.core")) else NA,       plotly.js = if (uses_core) js_version("plotly.core", "plotly.min.js") else js_version("plotly", "plotly-latest.min.js")     )   }, libpath = c(lib, .libPaths())) } py <- jsonlite::fromJSON(system2(python, c("-c", shQuote(paste(   "import json, plotly, numpy, pandas, plotly.offline as o;",   "print(json.dumps(dict(plotly=plotly.__version__, numpy=numpy.__version__,",   "pandas=pandas.__version__, plotlyjs=o.get_plotlyjs_version())))"))), stdout = TRUE)) versions <- rbindlist(list(   c(variant = "release", r_versions(release_lib)),   c(variant = "core_backend, go_figure_f32", r_versions(core_lib)),   list(variant = "plotly_py, plotly_py_f32",        plotly = paste0(py$plotly, " (Python; numpy ", py$numpy, ", pandas ", py$pandas, ")"),        plotly.core = NA_character_, plotly.js = py$plotlyjs) )) cpu <- if (Sys.info()[["sysname"]] == "Darwin") {   system("sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string", intern = TRUE) } else {   NA_character_ } meta <- list(date = format(Sys.Date()), R = R.version.string, os = utils::sessionInfo()$running,              cpu = cpu, browser = chrome$Browser$getVersion()$product, reps = reps) chrome$close()  fwrite(build, file.path(results_dir, "build.csv")) fwrite(browser, file.path(results_dir, "browser.csv")) fwrite(pages[, .(variant, case, size, values, html_mb)], file.path(results_dir, "pages.csv")) fwrite(versions, file.path(results_dir, "versions.csv")) jsonlite::write_json(meta, file.path(results_dir, "meta.json"), auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)

title: Rendering performance
text: Three use cases, range sizes: Large time series: one scattergl line trace date-time x (1 s steps) random walk y. 10 time series: ten scattergl line traces, one per column wide data.table, sharing date-time x. plotly.core sends array repeated figure (see widget_to_JSON()), x sent rather ten times. Large matrix heatmap: one heatmap trace n × n matrix. Metrics: Build + write (s): R Python time figure-making call standalone HTML page written disk (htmlwidgets::saveWidget() CRAN release, plotly.core’s write_html() plot_ly() development plotly go_figure(), fig.write_html() Python), one untimed warm-run, fresh process per variant. Image export (s): time save figure, made beforehand, 700 × 500 PNG package’s export (save_image() R; fig.write_image() plotly.py), one untimed warm-export, process build timings. covers converting figure JSON (including plotly_build() plot_ly() figures, built exported), drawing headless browser writing PNG; starting browser (done warm-, 1–1.5 s session’s first image) , go_figure() plotly.py, creating figure object. Kaleido (CRAN plotly, plotly.py) runs persistent server package’s plotly.js, plotly.core keeps Chrome running. HTML (MB): size page, holds figure data (plotly.js separate file). Load time (s): headless Chrome, navigation start first frame painted plotly.js’s newPlot() resolves. Pages served HTTP localhost browser cache disabled, time covers fetching parsing plotly.js page, decoding data plotting, network latency. newPlot (s): time plotly.js spends newPlot(), part load time. Peak renderer memory (MB): largest resident memory page’s renderer process loading, sampled every 20 ms. JS heap load (MB): JavaScript heap use load forced garbage collection, plus array buffers (Chrome reports ).

code: r_worker <- function(variant, fns, write, export, cases, reps, outdir) {   suppressPackageStartupMessages(     if (variant == "go_figure_f32") library(plotly.core) else library(plotly)   )   dir.create(outdir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)   out <- list()   for (i in seq_len(nrow(cases))) {     n <- cases$size[i]     v <- readBin(cases$file[i], "double", n = cases$values[i], endian = "little")     t <- as.POSIXct("2024-01-01", tz = "UTC") + seq_len(n) - 1     if (cases$case[i] == "timeseries") {       args <- list(t = t, y = v)     } else if (cases$case[i] == "multiseries") {       y <- matrix(v, n, 10, dimnames = list(NULL, sprintf("y%02d", 1:10)))       args <- list(d = data.table::data.table(t = t, y))     } else {       args <- list(z = matrix(v, n, n))     }     make <- fns[[cases$case[i]]]     page <- file.path(outdir, sprintf("%s-%d.html", cases$case[i], n))     save <- function() write(do.call(make, args), page)     save() # warm-up; also the page the browser loads     # static image export of a figure made beforehand, so only the export is timed     fig <- do.call(make, args)     png <- file.path(outdir, sprintf("%s-%d.png", cases$case[i], n))     export(fig, png) # warm-up     for (rep in seq_len(reps)) {       gc()       out[[length(out) + 1]] <- list(         variant = variant, case = cases$case[i], size = n, rep = rep,         build_sec = system.time(save())[["elapsed"]],         export_sec = system.time(export(fig, png))[["elapsed"]]       )     }   }   data.table::rbindlist(out) }  # Kaleido (for the CRAN release) runs in the benchmark's Python, which also # has plotly; ~/.Renviron is skipped, as it may point reticulate elsewhere worker_env <- c(callr::rcmd_safe_env(), RETICULATE_PYTHON = python, R_ENVIRON_USER = tempfile()) build_r <- rbindlist(lapply(names(figures), function(v) {   callr::r(r_worker, list(v, figures[[v]], writers[[v]], exporters[[v]], cases, reps, file.path(pages_dir, v)),            libpath = c(libs[[v]], .libPaths()), env = worker_env) })) cases_json <- file.path(wd, "cases.json") jsonlite::write_json(cases[, .(case, size, file)], cases_json) build_py <- rbindlist(lapply(c("plotly_py", "plotly_py_f32"), function(v) {   outdir <- file.path(pages_dir, v)   dir.create(outdir, showWarnings = FALSE)   res <- system2(python, c(shQuote(file.path(wd, "bench.py")), v, shQuote(cases_json), reps,                            shQuote(outdir)), stdout = TRUE)   as.data.table(jsonlite::fromJSON(paste(res, collapse = ""))) })) build <- rbindlist(list(build_r, build_py)) # one page per variant and case size pages <- CJ(variant = variants, i = seq_len(nrow(cases)), sorted = FALSE)[   , c(.(variant = variant), cases[i, .(case, size, values)])] pages[, path := sprintf("%s/%s-%d.html", variant, case, size)] pages[, html_mb := file.size(file.path(pages_dir, path)) / 1e6]

title: Rendering performance
text: script injected page script runs wraps plotly.js’s newPlot()/react()/plot() time first plot, marks first frame painted :
code: (function () {   var B = window.__bench = { done: false };   function finish() {     if (B.end != null) return;     B.end = performance.now();     requestAnimationFrame(function () {       setTimeout(function () { B.painted = performance.now(); B.done = true; }, 0);     });   }   // plotly.js 3+ exports are read-only, so the wrapper is a new object   // inheriting from Plotly, with timed newPlot()/react()/plot()   function wrap(P) {     if (!P || P.__benchWrapped) return P;     var W = Object.create(P);     ["newPlot", "react", "plot"].forEach(function (k) {       var orig = P[k];       if (typeof orig !== "function") return;       W[k] = function () {         if (B.start == null) B.start = performance.now();         var r = orig.apply(P, arguments);         Promise.resolve(r).then(finish, function (e) { B.error = String(e); B.done = true; });         return r;       };     });     W.__benchWrapped = true;     return W;   }   var plotly;   Object.defineProperty(window, "Plotly", {     configurable: true,     get: function () { return plotly; },     set: function (v) { plotly = wrap(v); }   });   window.addEventListener("error", function (e) { B.error = String(e.message); B.done = true; }); })(); hook_js <- paste(readLines(file.path(wd, "hook.js")), collapse = "\n") chrome <- chromote::Chromote$new()  # serve the pages over HTTP from localhost port <- httpuv::randomPort() server <- callr::r_bg(function(dir, port) httpuv::runStaticServer(dir, port = port, browse = FALSE),                       list(pages_dir, port)) for (i in 1:50) {   if (!inherits(try(suppressWarnings(readLines(sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d/", port), n = 1)),                     silent = TRUE), "try-error")) break   Sys.sleep(0.1) }  # samples the largest renderer process's memory (RSS) every 20 ms until killed sampler <- function(browser_pid, out) {   peak <- 0   writeLines("0", out) # started   repeat {     procs <- try(ps::ps_children(ps::ps_handle(browser_pid), recursive = TRUE), silent = TRUE)     if (!inherits(procs, "try-error")) {       for (p in procs) {         rss <- try({           if (any(grepl("--type=renderer", ps::ps_cmdline(p), fixed = TRUE))) ps::ps_memory_info(p)[["rss"]] else 0         }, silent = TRUE)         if (is.numeric(rss) && rss > peak) {           peak <- rss           writeLines(format(peak, scientific = FALSE), out)         }       }     }     Sys.sleep(0.02)   } } browser_pid <- chrome$get_browser()$get_process()$get_pid()  measure_page <- function(url, timeout = 300) {   s <- chromote::ChromoteSession$new(parent = chrome, width = 1000, height = 600)   on.exit(s$close(), add = TRUE)   s$Network$enable()   s$Network$setCacheDisabled(cacheDisabled = TRUE)   s$Page$enable() # needed for the injected script to run   s$Page$addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument(source = hook_js)   peak_file <- tempfile()   smp <- callr::r_bg(sampler, list(browser_pid, peak_file))   on.exit(smp$kill(), add = TRUE)   # wait for the sampler to start   for (i in 1:100) if (file.exists(peak_file)) break else Sys.sleep(0.05)   Sys.sleep(0.1)   s$Page$navigate(url, wait_ = FALSE) # large pages can take a while to commit   t0 <- Sys.time()   repeat {     done <- s$Runtime$evaluate("!!(window.__bench && window.__bench.done)", timeout_ = timeout)$result$value     if (isTRUE(done)) break     if (difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs") > timeout) stop("timed out loading ", url)     Sys.sleep(0.05)   }   Sys.sleep(0.3)   smp$kill()   b <- jsonlite::fromJSON(s$Runtime$evaluate(     "JSON.stringify(Object.assign({}, window.__bench, {js_bytes: performance.getEntriesByType('resource')        .filter(e => /\\.js$/.test(e.name)).reduce((a, e) => a + e.encodedBodySize, 0)}))"   )$result$value)   if (!is.null(b$error)) stop(url, ": ", b$error)   s$HeapProfiler$collectGarbage()   heap <- s$Runtime$getHeapUsage()   data.table(     load_sec = b$painted / 1000,     newplot_sec = (b$end - b$start) / 1000,     js_mb = b$js_bytes / 1e6,     peak_renderer_mb = as.numeric(readLines(peak_file, warn = FALSE)) / 1e6,     js_heap_mb = (heap$usedSize + if (is.null(heap$backingStorageSize)) 0 else heap$backingStorageSize) / 1e6   ) }  restart_chrome <- function() {   try(chrome$close(), silent = TRUE)   chrome <<- chromote::Chromote$new()   browser_pid <<- chrome$get_browser()$get_process()$get_pid() } # on a failure (e.g. Chrome not responding), restart Chrome and try the page # once more; a page that fails twice (e.g. too large to load) is recorded as # missing values, and not tried again in later rounds failed <- character() measure_retry <- function(url) {   missing <- data.table(load_sec = NA_real_, newplot_sec = NA_real_, js_mb = NA_real_,                         peak_renderer_mb = NA_real_, js_heap_mb = NA_real_)   if (url %in% failed) return(missing)   for (attempt in 1:2) {     r <- tryCatch(measure_page(url), error = identity)     if (!inherits(r, "error")) return(r)     message("attempt ", attempt, " at ", url, " failed: ", conditionMessage(r))     restart_chrome()   }   failed <<- c(failed, url)   missing }  set.seed(1) browser <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(reps), function(rep) {   # shuffle the page order each round, so drift doesn't favour a variant   rbindlist(lapply(sample(nrow(pages)), function(i) {     cbind(pages[i, .(variant, case, size)], rep = rep,           measure_retry(sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d/%s", port, pages$path[i])))   })) })) server$kill()

numpy ", py$numpy, ", pandas ", py$pandas, ")"),        plotly.core = NA_character_, plotly.js = py$plotlyjs) )) cpu <- if (Sys.info()[["sysname"]] == "Darwin") {   system("sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string", intern = TRUE) } else {   NA_character_ } meta <- list(date = format(Sys.Date()), R = R.version.string, os = utils::sessionInfo()$running,              cpu = cpu, browser = chrome$Browser$getVersion()$product, reps = reps) chrome$close()  fwrite(build, file.path(results_dir, "build.csv")) fwrite(browser, file.path(results_dir, "browser.csv")) fwrite(pages[, .(variant, case, size, values, html_mb)], file.path(results_dir, "pages.csv")) fwrite(versions, file.path(results_dir, "versions.csv")) jsonlite::write_json(meta, file.path(results_dir, "meta.json"), auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)

title: Streaming data with plotlyProxy()
text: app plots sine cosine time (seconds since 1970) last 60 seconds, adding point trace ten times second. arguments "extendTraces" Plotly.extendTraces(gd, update, indices, maxPoints): () keeps one-value vectors arrays (["2026-11-17 12:00:00.100"]), extendTraces needs: plain length-one vectors sent single values.
code: library(shiny) library(plotly.core)  window <- 60 # seconds shown rate <- 10 # points per second n <- window * rate # points kept per trace  # Times as plotly.js date strings (local time, with milliseconds) stamp <- function(t) format(t, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS3")  ui <- fluidPage(plotlyOutput("stream"))  server <- function(input, output, session) {   # Rendered once: the last 60 seconds, so the window starts full   output$stream <- renderPlotly({     t <- Sys.time() - seq(window, 0, length.out = n)     go_figure() |>       add_scatter(x = stamp(t), y = sin(as.numeric(t)), mode = "lines", name = "sin(t)") |>       add_scatter(x = stamp(t), y = cos(as.numeric(t)), mode = "lines", name = "cos(t)") |>       update_layout(yaxis = go_yaxis(range = c(-1.1, 1.1)))   })    proxy <- plotlyProxy("stream", session)    # Ten times a second: one new point for each trace, keeping the last n   observe({     invalidateLater(1000 / rate)     t <- Sys.time()     s <- as.numeric(t)     plotlyProxyInvoke(       proxy,       "extendTraces",       list(x = list(I(stamp(t)), I(stamp(t))), y = list(I(sin(s)), I(cos(s)))),       I(c(0L, 1L)),       n     )   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Streaming data with plotlyProxy()
text: plot runs update plain JavaScript, without Shiny, can see result straight away: trace keeps 600 points, window moves, zooming hiding trace isn’t undone updates.
code: library(plotly.core) fig <- go_figure() |>   add_scatter(x = character(), y = numeric(), mode = "lines", name = "sin(t)") |>   add_scatter(x = character(), y = numeric(), mode = "lines", name = "cos(t)") |>   update_layout(height = 350, yaxis = go_yaxis(range = c(-1.1, 1.1)), xaxis = go_xaxis(type = "date")) htmlwidgets::onRender(as_widget(fig), " function(el) {   var n = 600, step = 100;   var pad = function(v, w) { return String(v).padStart(w || 2, '0'); };   var stamp = function(d) {     return d.getFullYear() + '-' + pad(d.getMonth() + 1) + '-' + pad(d.getDate()) + ' ' +       pad(d.getHours()) + ':' + pad(d.getMinutes()) + ':' + pad(d.getSeconds()) + '.' +       pad(d.getMilliseconds(), 3);   };   // fill the window with the last 60 seconds, then add a point every 100 ms   var now = Date.now(), x = [], s = [], c = [];   for (var i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {     var t = now - i * step;     x.push(stamp(new Date(t))); s.push(Math.sin(t / 1000)); c.push(Math.cos(t / 1000));   }   Plotly.extendTraces(el, {x: [x, x.slice()], y: [s, c]}, [0, 1], n);   setInterval(function() {     var t = Date.now(), d = stamp(new Date(t));     Plotly.extendTraces(el, {x: [[d], [d]], y: [[Math.sin(t / 1000)], [Math.cos(t / 1000)]]}, [0, 1], n);   }, step); }")

title: Streaming data with plotlyProxy()
text: approach works trace type arrays extend. app draws two spirals polar plot: angle point time modulo 2π, radians (thetaunit = "radians" traces; turn takes 2π ≈ 6.3 seconds), second spiral quarter turn ahead, radius seconds since session started. rangemode = "normal" radial axis covers just last 60 seconds, newest points edge spiral winds inwards oldest, 9.5 turns. browser:
code: library(shiny) library(plotly.core)  window <- 60 # seconds shown rate <- 10 # points per second n <- window * rate # points kept per trace  ui <- fluidPage(plotlyOutput("spiral", height = "500px"))  server <- function(input, output, session) {   t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - window # the radius counts seconds from here    output$spiral <- renderPlotly({     s <- seq(t0, t0 + window, length.out = n) # the last 60 seconds     go_figure() |>       add_scatterpolar(r = s - t0, theta = s %% (2 * pi), thetaunit = "radians",                        mode = "lines", name = "t mod 2π") |>       add_scatterpolar(r = s - t0, theta = (s + pi / 2) %% (2 * pi), thetaunit = "radians",                        mode = "lines", name = "(t + π/2) mod 2π") |>       update_layout(polar = go_polar(         angularaxis = go_polar_angularaxis(thetaunit = "radians"), # axis labels in radians too         radialaxis = go_polar_radialaxis(rangemode = "normal") # not from 0: the last 60 seconds       ))   })    proxy <- plotlyProxy("spiral", session)    observe({     invalidateLater(1000 / rate)     s <- as.numeric(Sys.time())     plotlyProxyInvoke(       proxy,       "extendTraces",       list(         r = list(I(s - t0), I(s - t0)),         theta = list(I(s %% (2 * pi)), I((s + pi / 2) %% (2 * pi)))       ),       I(c(0L, 1L)),       n     )   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server) spiral <- go_figure() |>   add_scatterpolar(r = numeric(), theta = numeric(), thetaunit = "radians", mode = "lines",                    name = "t mod 2π") |>   add_scatterpolar(r = numeric(), theta = numeric(), thetaunit = "radians", mode = "lines",                    name = "(t + π/2) mod 2π") |>   update_layout(height = 500, polar = go_polar(     angularaxis = go_polar_angularaxis(thetaunit = "radians"),     radialaxis = go_polar_radialaxis(rangemode = "normal")   )) htmlwidgets::onRender(as_widget(spiral), " function(el) {   var n = 600, step = 100, t0 = Date.now() / 1000 - 60, tau = 2 * Math.PI;   var mod = function(a) { return ((a % tau) + tau) % tau; };   var r = [], a = [], b = [];   for (var i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) {     var s = Date.now() / 1000 - i * step / 1000;     r.push(s - t0); a.push(mod(s)); b.push(mod(s + Math.PI / 2));   }   Plotly.extendTraces(el, {r: [r, r.slice()], theta: [a, b]}, [0, 1], n);   setInterval(function() {     var s = Date.now() / 1000;     Plotly.extendTraces(el, {r: [[s - t0], [s - t0]], theta: [[mod(s)], [mod(s + Math.PI / 2)]]}, [0, 1], n);   }, step); }")

title: Streaming data with plotlyProxy()
text: 3D traces (scatter3d) drawn WebGL, like scattergl, extended way. app draws path x = sin(t), y = cos(t), z = tan(t) last 5 seconds, marker tip. two traces keep different numbers points: maxPoints can give attribute trace limit, 50 points path 1 marker. tan(t) jumps +∞ −∞ time t passes π/2 + kπ. missing value (NA, sent null) jump stops path drawing line across plot , axis ranges fixed view doesn’t rescale path moves. view can rotated (drag) zoomed (scroll) data stream: widget keeps current view update, holds updates 3D plot dragged scrolled, applying let go (update drag undo ). browser:
code: library(shiny) library(plotly.core)  window <- 5 # seconds shown rate <- 10 # points per second n <- window * rate # points kept on the path  # tan(s) jumps from +Inf to -Inf where s passes pi/2 + k * pi: k, the branch branch <- function(s) floor(s / pi + 0.5)  # The path at times s, with a gap (NA) before each point on a new branch path <- function(s) {   copies <- 1 + c(FALSE, diff(branch(s)) != 0)   t <- rep(s, copies)   gap <- duplicated(rep(seq_along(s), copies), fromLast = TRUE)   list(     x = ifelse(gap, NA, sin(t)),     y = ifelse(gap, NA, cos(t)),     z = ifelse(gap, NA, tan(t))   ) }  # a square plot (up to 700 px wide) ui <- fluidPage(div(style = "max-width: 700px", plotlyOutput("path3d", height = "700px")))  server <- function(input, output, session) {   last <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) # time of the newest point    output$path3d <- renderPlotly({     s <- last - seq(window, 0, length.out = n)     p <- path(s)     go_figure() |>       add_scatter3d(x = p$x, y = p$y, z = p$z, mode = "lines", name = "path") |>       add_scatter3d(x = I(sin(last)), y = I(cos(last)), z = I(tan(last)),                     mode = "markers", marker = go_scatter3d_marker(size = 6), name = "tip") |>       update_layout(         scene = go_scene(           xaxis = go_scene_axis(range = c(-1.1, 1.1)),           yaxis = go_scene_axis(range = c(-1.1, 1.1)),           zaxis = go_scene_axis(range = c(-10, 10)),           aspectmode = "cube"         ),         legend = go_legend(orientation = "h", y = 1, yanchor = "bottom"), # above the plot         margin = go_margin(l = 0, r = 0, t = 30, b = 0)       )   })    proxy <- plotlyProxy("path3d", session)    observe({     invalidateLater(1000 / rate)     s <- as.numeric(Sys.time())     p <- lapply(path(c(last, s)), `[`, -1) # the new point, after a gap if any     last <<- s     plotlyProxyInvoke(       proxy,       "extendTraces",       list(         x = list(I(p$x), I(sin(s))),         y = list(I(p$y), I(cos(s))),         z = list(I(p$z), I(tan(s)))       ),       I(c(0L, 1L)),       # per attribute, the points kept by each trace: n on the path, 1 tip       list(x = c(n, 1L), y = c(n, 1L), z = c(n, 1L))     )   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server) path3d <- go_figure() |>   add_scatter3d(x = numeric(), y = numeric(), z = numeric(), mode = "lines", name = "path") |>   add_scatter3d(x = numeric(), y = numeric(), z = numeric(), mode = "markers",                 marker = go_scatter3d_marker(size = 6), name = "tip") |>   update_layout(     height = 700,     legend = go_legend(orientation = "h", y = 1, yanchor = "bottom"),     margin = go_margin(l = 0, r = 0, t = 30, b = 0),     scene = go_scene(       xaxis = go_scene_axis(range = c(-1.1, 1.1)),       yaxis = go_scene_axis(range = c(-1.1, 1.1)),       zaxis = go_scene_axis(range = c(-10, 10)),       aspectmode = "cube"     )   ) htmlwidgets::onRender(as_widget(path3d), " function(el) {   var n = 50, step = 100;   var branch = function(s) { return Math.floor(s / Math.PI + 0.5); };   var last = Date.now() / 1000 - 5;   // the new point at time s, after a gap (null) where tan(s) changes branch   var points = function(s) {     var p = {x: [], y: [], z: []};     if (branch(s) !== branch(last)) { p.x.push(null); p.y.push(null); p.z.push(null); }     p.x.push(Math.sin(s)); p.y.push(Math.cos(s)); p.z.push(Math.tan(s));     last = s;     return p;   };   // as the widget does for proxy calls: no updates while the view is being   // rotated or zoomed, and the current view kept through each update   var held = false, wheelUntil = 0;   el.addEventListener('pointerdown', function() { held = true; }, true);   window.addEventListener('pointerup', function() { held = false; });   el.addEventListener('wheel', function() { wheelUntil = Date.now() + 400; }, true);   var add = function(s) {     var p = points(s);     var scene = el._fullLayout && el._fullLayout.scene && el._fullLayout.scene._scene;     if (scene) el.layout.scene.camera = scene.getCamera();     Plotly.extendTraces(el,       {x: [p.x, [Math.sin(s)]], y: [p.y, [Math.cos(s)]], z: [p.z, [Math.tan(s)]]},       [0, 1], {x: [n, 1], y: [n, 1], z: [n, 1]});   };   for (var i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) add(Date.now() / 1000 - i * step / 1000);   setInterval(function() {     if (held || Date.now() < wheelUntil) return;     // catch up on the points held back, one every 100 ms     var now = Date.now() / 1000;     for (var t = Math.max(last + step / 1000, now - 5); t <= now; t += step / 1000) add(t);   }, step); }")

text: heatmap can stream . x axis time (last 60 seconds), y axis runs 0 2π, colour sin(y) · cos(t mod 2π), column sine wave scaled time 2π-second cycle. Ten times second app adds column. extendTraces appends arrays, heatmap’s z array rows. transpose = TRUE row z column heatmap (one time), new time one new row: z = list(list(column)) adds column trace 0, maxPoints keeps last 600 times. zmin zmax fix colour scale, colours don’t shift range data window changes. browser:
code: library(shiny) library(plotly.core)  window <- 60 # seconds shown rate <- 10 # columns per second n <- window * rate # columns kept y <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 61)  stamp <- function(t) format(t, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS3") # The column at time t: sin(y) * cos(t mod 2 pi) column <- function(t) sin(y) * cos(as.numeric(t) %% (2 * pi))  ui <- fluidPage(plotlyOutput("heat"))  server <- function(input, output, session) {   output$heat <- renderPlotly({     times <- Sys.time() - seq(window, 0, length.out = n)     go_figure() |>       add_heatmap(         x = stamp(times),         y = y,         z = t(vapply(times, column, numeric(length(y)))), # a row per time         transpose = TRUE, # rows of z are columns of the heatmap         zmin = -1,         zmax = 1,         colorscale = "RdBu"       ) |>       update_layout(yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "y (radians)"))   })    proxy <- plotlyProxy("heat", session)    observe({     invalidateLater(1000 / rate)     t <- Sys.time()     plotlyProxyInvoke(       proxy,       "extendTraces",       list(x = list(I(stamp(t))), z = list(list(column(t)))),       I(0L),       n     )   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server) heat <- go_figure() |>   add_heatmap(x = character(), y = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 61), z = list(),               transpose = TRUE, zmin = -1, zmax = 1, colorscale = "RdBu") |>   update_layout(height = 400, yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "y (radians)"), xaxis = go_xaxis(type = "date")) htmlwidgets::onRender(as_widget(heat), " function(el) {   var n = 600, step = 100, tau = 2 * Math.PI, y = [];   for (var j = 0; j <= 60; j++) y.push(j / 60 * tau);   var pad = function(v, w) { return String(v).padStart(w || 2, '0'); };   var stamp = function(d) {     return d.getFullYear() + '-' + pad(d.getMonth() + 1) + '-' + pad(d.getDate()) + ' ' +       pad(d.getHours()) + ':' + pad(d.getMinutes()) + ':' + pad(d.getSeconds()) + '.' +       pad(d.getMilliseconds(), 3);   };   // the column at time t (ms): sin(y) * cos(t mod 2 pi)   var column = function(t) {     var c = Math.cos(((t / 1000) % tau + tau) % tau);     return y.map(function(v) { return Math.sin(v) * c; });   };   var now = Date.now(), x = [], z = [];   for (var i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) { var t = now - i * step; x.push(stamp(new Date(t))); z.push(column(t)); }   Plotly.extendTraces(el, {x: [x], z: [z]}, [0], n);   setInterval(function() {     var t = Date.now();     Plotly.extendTraces(el, {x: [[stamp(new Date(t))]], z: [[column(t)]]}, [0], n);   }, step); }")
